info.label: Intro
notes:
Welcome everyone — great to have you here.

Today we’ll spend about 90 minutes on Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat — and more importantly, how to actually use it effectively in your daily work.

info.label: Narration
notes:
Quick setup:

- Feel free to turn on your camera if you like
- Please stay muted during the session
- Ask questions anytime in chat
- We’ll have time for Q&A at the end

info.label: Interaction
notes:
We’ll also use reactions:
👍 = yes
😲 = no

Quick check — who has already used Copilot?

info.label: Segue
notes: Let’s start with the basics — what Copilot actually is.

info.label: Narration 1
notes:
Copilot is an AI assistant.

But — and this is important — it’s still just an assistant.

It doesn’t magically know what you want.

You need to tell it clearly what you want.

info.label: Narration 2
notes:
And that leads to one key principle:

Better prompt → better result.

info.label: Narration 3
notes:
Copilot is trained on large language models.

That data is static.

So how do we get current or company-specific data?

That’s where grounding comes in.

Grounding means adding context to the model.

Two types:
- Web grounding → internet
- Work grounding → your company data

info.label: Demo
notes:
Let me show you where all of this happens.

Go to m365copilot.com.

If you remember one thing today — it’s this URL.

This is your entry point into Copilot Chat.

info.label: Segue
notes: Now that we understand what Copilot is — let’s talk about how to actually get good results from it.

info.label: Narration 1
notes:
Copilot is powerful — but only as good as your prompt.

If your input is vague, your output will be vague.

info.label: Narration 2
notes:
Think of prompts in four parts:

1. Goal
2. Context
3. Instructions
4. Output format

info.label: Demo 1
notes:
Let’s start with a bad example.

Write an email.

This is too vague — Copilot doesn’t know what you want.

info.label: Demo 2
notes:
Now let’s improve it step by step.

Write a professional email to a customer declining a request, polite tone, 5 sentences.

Much better — now Copilot has direction.

info.label: Interaction
notes:
What do you think is missing in the first prompt?

Let’s build a better one together.

info.label: Segue
notes: Now let’s move from basics to real-world usage.

info.label: Narration 1
notes:
Copilot is not just one tool.

You’ll find it in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook.

Same AI — different context.

info.label: Narration 2
notes:
You can share Copilot conversations.

Think of them as reusable knowledge.

info.label: Demo 1
notes:
Let me show you how sharing works.

You can send this conversation to a colleague — and they can continue from there.

info.label: Narration 3
notes:
Copilot Pages turn chats into structured documents.

This is where things become reusable.

info.label: Narration 4
notes:
And then we have agents.

Instead of prompting every time — you define behavior once.

info.label: Break
notes:
Let’s take a short 5-minute break.

When we come back, we’ll wrap up and take your questions.

info.label: Narration
notes:
If you remember three things:

1. Copilot is an assistant — be specific
2. Prompt quality matters
3. Grounding is where the value is

info.label: Q&A
notes:
Let’s open it up.

What questions do you have?
